bank.keyText: Fermentation uses no electron transport chain and builds no proton gradient
choiceTexts: Fermentation uses a chain too, but with oxygen as the final acceptor
Fermentation uses no electron transport chain and builds no proton gradient
It produces less ATP per glucose than fermentation does
Fermentation passes electrons to nitrate, while anaerobic respiration passes them to pyruvate
It is the same process under a different name

answer.text: Fermentation uses no electron transport chain and builds no proton gradient
answer.line: Both run without oxygen, but only anaerobic respiration keeps a membrane chain and a gradient. Fermentation has neither.

steps: Ask where the electrons from NADH go. That one question splits the two.
Anaerobic respiration sends them down a membrane chain to sulfate or nitrate. The chain builds a gradient that drives ATP synthase.
Fermentation hands them straight to an organic molecule, pyruvate or acetaldehyde. No chain, no gradient, only the 2 ATP from glycolysis.

choices.text: Fermentation uses a chain too, but with oxygen as the final acceptor
choices.note: A chain that ends at oxygen is aerobic respiration. Fermentation has no chain at all.

choices.text: Fermentation uses no electron transport chain and builds no proton gradient
choices.note: No chain and no gradient: that is the line between them.

choices.text: It produces less ATP per glucose than fermentation does
choices.note: A chain plus a gradient out-earns fermentation, which keeps only the 2 ATP from glycolysis. Anaerobic respiration makes more, not less.

choices.text: Fermentation passes electrons to nitrate, while anaerobic respiration passes them to pyruvate
choices.note: This swaps the two acceptors. The stem itself hands nitrate and sulfate to the bacteria with the chain.

choices.text: It is the same process under a different name
choices.note: Both run without oxygen, which is why they blur together. One uses a membrane chain and a gradient; the other does not.

lockIt: Anaerobic respiration keeps the chain and the gradient; fermentation has neither.
